chapter_title: Concerning the Wheel that exists in front of the King of Honour
chapter_note: This chapter is overwhelmingly systematic cosmological exposition about the Wheel before the King of Honour in the seventh firmament, functioning as a binding/diagnostic device over the rulers and powers. Only the opening dialogue attribution (“apostle speaks”) is a later framing tag; the rest maintains an impersonal, structural voice and stays within the cosmic architecture (firmaments, rulers, zone, fetter, seals, shining men). Paragraph 5’s simile (chain/guard) is a generic illustrative comparison and does not clearly anchor to institutional or NT material, though it may be a secondary explanatory gloss.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.88⟩
[Agai]n the [...] the wheel that exists in front [of the King of Honour who dwells in] the seventh firmament [...], the root of the rulers above and below in a great and cruel fetter; as the entire will of the great King of Honour is placed in [it]. Also, their entire enmity, which is in the firmaments, is [...] and ensnared in it.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue/frame attribution “the [apostl]e speaks” (Layer-2 compilation frame; ‘apostle’ must not appear in core_text).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opening contains a formulaic attribution (“Again … the apostle speaks”), but the remaining clause-set is impersonal, cosmological mechanism: wheel–seventh firmament–root of rulers–fetter/ensnaring; no audience address or institutional targeting.

paragraphs.core_text: It exists in a blaze of splendour [with] ornamentation and great beauty. Now, there are twelve seals in it. The seal between i[s] every firmament and the rulers who are there [... ...] are in it; for should one of them wish to escape, he will be bound [...]. If he should wish to cause a trick in his bond [... will be] apparent and known in [that] wheel [...]. The spheres and stars and [the] leader of all the powers exist there, and can be known by it, in front of the King of Honour.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic description of the wheel’s structure (twelve seals) and its cosmic function (detecting escape/trick of rulers; relation to firmaments/spheres/stars) in an expository voice—no citations, no pastoral address.

paragraphs.core_text: The twelf[t]h seal that is in it is its five shining men that are conjoined and enmeshed through the entire zone; because every place where they are cramped, and every place where they have space, is displayed by that wheel. For the root of all the firmaments above and below, and that of their rulers, is ensnared and fixed in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Numbered/structural cosmology (twelfth seal; five shining men; zone) with functional mechanics (display/ensnare/fix). This is characteristic of the older teaching substrate’s degree-mapping style.

paragraphs.core_text: The observation [...] is set right at all times opposite the great King o[f Honour ...] so that fear, wh[ich ...] will assume all the powers of mixture [... ...] their root affixed there, so that they cannot make an esc[a]pe from the fetter of their bond.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continues impersonal mechanism: “observation” set opposite the King of Honour; “powers of mixture” constrained; no shift to exhortation or contemporary institutions.

paragraphs.core_text: That wheel rese[m]bles, in this respect, a chain in front of the chief guard, for when [...] in th[ose ...] in the [... cha]in.
paragraphs.temporal_note: A brief simile (wheel ~ chain/guard) used to clarify the binding function. It does not invoke church structures, polemic ‘today’, or NT citation; however, because it uses a worldly analogy rather than intra-cosmic mapping, it could be a secondary explanatory gloss.

paragraphs.core_text: This is also the case for all the rulers who are in the firmaments, and every power of the zone: If they should wish to escape, they shall be recognised and revealed by that wheel. [As] the wheel is like a great mirror, for [the di]scrimination of all things [... is] in it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Generalizing conclusion in the same cosmological register (rulers/firmaments/zone) with correspondential analogy (mirror) to describe cognition/discrimination—still internal to the cosmic system and not framed as moral instruction.
